arxiv-2305-19640.title: Fine-grained analysis of non-parametric estimation for pairwise learning
arxiv-2305-19640.creator: Junyu Zhou, Shuo Huang, Han Feng, Puyu Wang, Ding-Xuan Zhou
arxiv-2305-19640.description: Abstract In this paper, we are concerned with the generalization performance of non-parametric estimation for pairwise learning. Most of the existing work requires the hypothesis space to be convex or a VC-class, and the loss to be convex. However, these restrictive assumptions limit the applicability of the results in studying many popular methods, especially kernel methods and neural networks.

arxiv-2306-11438.title: F F -invariant in cluster algebras
arxiv-2306-11438.creator: Peigen Cao
arxiv-2306-11438.description: Abstract . In this paper, we introduce the F F -invariant in cluster algebras using tropicalization. This is an analog of the E E -invariant introduced by Derksen, Weyman and Zelevinsky in the additive categorification of cluster algebras and the 𝔡 \mathfrak{d} -invariant introduced by Kang, Kashiwara, Kim and Oh in the monoidal categorification of (quantum) cluster algebras.

arxiv-2306-15445.title: UniUD Submission to the EPIC-Kitchens-100 Multi-Instance Retrieval Challenge 2023
arxiv-2306-15445.creator: Alex Falcon, Giuseppe Serra
arxiv-2306-15445.description: Abstract In this report, we present the technical details of our submission to the EPIC-Kitchens-100 Multi-Instance Retrieval Challenge 2023. To participate in the challenge, we ensembled two models trained with two different loss functions on 25% of the training data. Our submission, visible on the public leaderboard, obtains an average score of 56.81% nDCG and 42.63% mAP.

arxiv-2404-16399.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning with Behavioral Supervisor Tuning
arxiv-2404-16399.creator: Padmanaba Srinivasan, William Knottenbelt
arxiv-2404-16399.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Padmanaba Srinivasan, William Knottenbelt. Offline reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are applied to learn performant, well-generalizing policies when provided with a static dataset of interactions. Many recent approaches to offline RL have seen substantial success, but with one key caveat: they demand substantial per-dataset hyperparameter tuning to achieve reported perf ormance, which requires policy rollouts in the environment to evaluate; this can rapidly become cumbersome. Furthermore, substantial tuning requirements can hamper the adoption of these algorithms in practical domains.

arxiv-2410-05217.title: Organizing Unstructured Image Collections using Natural Language
arxiv-2410-05217.creator: Mingxuan Liu Zhun Zhong Jun Li Gianni Franchi Subhankar Roy Elisa Ricci
arxiv-2410-05217.description: Abstract Organizing unstructured image collections into semantic clusters is a long-standing challenge. Traditional deep clustering techniques address this by producing a single data partition, whereas multiple clustering methods uncover diverse alternative partitions, but only when users predefine the clustering criteria. Yet expecting users to specify such criteria a priori for large, unfamiliar datasets is unrealistic.

arxiv-2504-04375.title: Self-Guided Diffusion Model for Accelerating Computational Fluid Dynamics
arxiv-2504-04375.creator: Ruoyan Li, Zijie Huang, Haixin Wang, Guancheng Wan, Yizhou Sun, Wei Wang
arxiv-2504-04375.description: Abstract . Machine learning methods, such as diffusion models, are widely explored as a promising way to accelerate high-fidelity fluid dynamics computation via a super-resolution process from faster-to-compute low-fidelity input. However, existing approaches usually make impractical assumptions that the low-fidelity data is down-sampled from high-fidelity data. In reality, low-fidelity data is produced by numerical solvers that use a coarser resolution.

arxiv-2505-20534.title: Quantum Resilience: Canadian Innovations in Quantum Error Correction and Quantum Error Mitigation
arxiv-2505-20534.creator: Gaurav Saxena, Jack S. Baker, Pablo Díez Valle, William E. Salazar, Kevin Ferreira, Thi Ha Kyaw
arxiv-2505-20534.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gaurav Saxena, Jack S. Baker, Pablo Díez Valle, William E. Salazar, Kevin Ferreira, Thi Ha Kyaw. In celebration of the 2025 International Year of Quantum Science and Technology, this article highlights the pioneering achievements and ongoing innovations in quantum error correction and quantum error mitigation by Canadian institutions, academia and industry alike. Emphasizing Canada’s central role in advancing these two related areas, we summarize landmark theoretical breakthroughs, cutting-edge experiments, and emerging techniques aimed at reducing and/or eliminating errors incurred when using a quantum computer.

pmc-11355022.title: Photosynthesis: Genetic Strategies Adopted to Gain Higher Efficiency
pmc-11355022.creator: Naveed Khan, Seok-Hyun Choi, Choon-Hwan Lee, Mingnan Qu, Jong-Seong Jeon, Joanna Grzyb
pmc-11355022.description: The global challenge of feeding an ever-increasing population to maintain food security requires novel approaches to increase crop yields. Evaluating the operational status of the photosynthetic mechanism provides insights into plants’ capacity to adapt to their surroundings.

This aspect is mainly due to the complexity of management in pediatric practice.

pmc-12553393.title: Emerging Role of Plant-Derived Nanostructures in Nanomedicine
pmc-12553393.creator: Huijie Xing, Guichan Li, Chunli Qi, Ming Zhang, Ning Ding, Xingwang Zhang
pmc-12553393.description: Plant-derived nanostructures (PDNSs) represent a promising class of natural nanomedicines that integrate therapeutic and drug delivery functions. These self-assembled nanosystems, including nanoparticles, nanovesicles, exosomes, and nanofibers, leverage bioactive phytoconstituents to overcome limitations of synthetic biomaterials, such as immunogenicity and suboptimal targeting. PDNSs exhibit unique advantages like high biocompatibility, autonomous formation, and multi-modal functionality.

pmc-13006216.title: CD39 in the pathogenesis of neuro-Behçet disease: is it an immune regulator marker?
pmc-13006216.creator: Khadija Bahrini, Amani Stiti, Sana Boughariou, Meriam Belghith
pmc-13006216.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Neuro-Behçet’s disease (NBD) is a severe neurological manifestation of Behçet’s disease (BD), a multisystemic inflammatory vasculitis affecting multiple organs. NBD presents complex immunopathological features involving both innate and adaptive immune responses. CD39 (ectonucleoside triphosphate diphosphohydrolase-1, ENTPD1), an ectoenzyme expressed on various immune cells, has emerged as a critical regulator of inflammation through its role in hydrolyzing extracellular ATP to immunosuppressive adenosine.
